function: Channel prediction at the BS (RNN, BiLSTM, NeuralProphet, hybrid) enabling CSI feedback of only the quantized predicted-minus-estimated difference, with no ML at the UE (pp. 1, 6).
system: Massive MIMO BS with M=64 antennas on a rooftop, single-antenna UE (monopole), FDD; 2.18 GHz carrier, 10 MHz OFDM (600 subcarriers); no RIS (pp. 2, 8).
method: Supervised RNN, BiLSTM, NeuralProphet and hybrid RNN+NP predictors trained at the BS (Huber loss, Adam, grid-searched hyperparameters); pseudo-inverse predictor function sent to UEs (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: Measured data: Nokia Bell-Labs campus, Stuttgart, 64-antenna BS, 2.18 GHz, 2000 samples/s; multiuser: synthetic AR channels; CsiNet comparison: nrCDLChannel, 15k samples (pp. 8-9, 12).
test_conditions: Trained on track-1 (116k CSI, 80/10/10 split); evaluated on tracks 1, 2, 12, stated unseen in training; multiuser uses synthetic AR data (pp. 9-10).
baselines: Non-learned: conventional feedback without ML, periodic round-robin feedback. Learned: MLaBE (ML at both ends, [3]), CsiNet autoencoder [8], standalone RNN, BiLSTM, NeuralProphet predictors (pp. 8, 10-12).
metrics: NMSE (channel predictors and feedback), cosine similarity, precoding gain, overhead bits, floating-point operations (pp. 9-12).
complexity: FLOPs for single-step prediction: CSILaBS 5.8 M versus CsiNet 58.52 M; 4 versus 32 layers; 4096 parameters reported (CSILaBS) versus 0.35 M (MLaBE) (pp. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 8: "a measurement campaign was performed at Nokia Bell-Labs campus in" Stuttgart; the channel predictors are trained and tested on this measured data (p. 9). p. 12: the CsiNet comparison data are generated with nrCDLChannel.
q2_support: p. 9: "which were unseen by the CPs during the training" phase: Fig. 6 (p. 10) tests tracks 1, 2 and 12, while training used only track-1 (p. 9: "To train CPs, we used dataset of track-1").
q3_support: p. 12: "with state-of-the-art, i.e., autoencoder [8], named CsiNet in" [8]: gains of about 43% in cosine similarity and 5.5 dB in NMSE at 2 bits; p. 10: "with two other schemes, i.e., MLaBE and without ML" (non-learned feedback without ML, NMSE and precoding gain).
q4_support: p. 12: "the number of floating-point operations for single-step prediction of CSILaBS are 5.8 M", against 58.52 M for CsiNet; p. 11: MLaBE needs 0.35 M parameters to report against M x M = 4096.
q5_support: p. 8: "a measurement campaign was performed at Nokia Bell-Labs campus in" Stuttgart; training and testing use this measured data. No code or data link is given; "details of the dataset are available in [5]" (p. 9) only points to a description.
notes: PDF is arXiv:2403.13363v1 (20 Mar 2024), 'Massive MIMO CSI Feedback using Channel Prediction: How to Avoid Machine Learning at UE?' (Shehzad, Rose, Assaad), marked accepted in IEEE TWC; the DOI is not printed in the text. Area 2: the learned predictor serves CSI feedback; the Glauber-based feedback selection (pp. 6-7) is not learned. q5 rests on measured data only, with no code or data link; reviewer to confirm. q2: Fig. 6 shows tracks 1, 2 and 12 and track 1 is the training track, so only tracks 2 and 12 are clearly other tracks. nrCDLChannel is MATLAB's CDL model (3GPP TR 38.901), not stated in the paper. MLaBE is the earlier approach of [3] by the same authors.
